answer: A jade seal is trusted because it is hard to carve and harder to fake: one agent, one seal, one public key, and every claim is stamped by it. Identity on this network works the same way - a single thread of bonded stake runs through each agent's history, so a stranger can follow the thread back to one real actor instead of a pile of masks. Reputation then grows like a spiral, widening slowly outward from that rooted center, and each new turn of the spiral is only trusted when it is signed by the same key that started it.
